body: Quick pass: merges cleanly with main; body complete; the author's post suites, app lathe suites and clippy are green on f65044b0. The quick gate's only red is `coarse_laws`, which fails the same way on main (refusal text changed by PR #1074; tracked as #1175). Flagged ready; posted G-code, so it gets the high-tier review now.

<!-- pr-reviewer: f65044b04982b50df705fc22cd1432b5fb80f92f -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge.** No blockers found. I read this adversarially (it changes posted G-code) and every attack below held.

### What I built and ran
Head f65044b0, trial-merged with origin/main 26cb6ac9 in its own worktree. The merge was clean; the only incoming changes were the Doosan files from #1159, which this PR does not touch.

| Run | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all 21 binaries, lib included) | all green; `recorded_streams` 11, each `script_*` 10, `post_engine` 33 |
| app `lathe_post` 7, `lathe_post_css` 10, `lathe_post_tormach` 8, `lathe_post_refusals` 11, `lathe_workholding_rpm` 5, `c_axis_live` 5, `c_axis_unwind` 7, `lathe_cycle_exit` 6, `lathe_spindle_law` 8, `conformance` 6, `golden_cl` 25, `solid_law_goldens` 5 | all green |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| **Fix reverted locally** (the two `if (cssOn) block(["G97"])` lines, never committed) | **9 pinning tests fail**: `lathe_post_refusals` 4 (live, thread, drill, two-CSS), `lathe_post_tormach` 3, `lathe_post_css` 1 (`facing_css.nc` golden), `script_fanuc_lathe::css_then_live` 1. With the fix restored they pass. |

I did not run the known-red `coarse_laws` suite or the xtask gate-map test. Nothing else was red.

### Exit paths: is `G97` always written after a G96 section?
- `cssOn` is set only where `G96 S.. M03` is actually written: `fanuc-lathe.cps:410-411`, `tormach-lathe.cps:392`. An unclamped G96 is refused, so the flag stays false. The flag is cleared at the same place it is used: `fanuc-lathe.cps:471-473`, `tormach-lathe.cps:426-428`.
- **Normal end, tool change, same tool, program end:** every turning section passes through `endPreamble`, which always writes `M05` / `M5` (the spindle never runs on into the next section, same tool or not), followed by `G97`. `onClose` calls `endPreamble` first, so a legacy stream with no SECTION records is covered too. The only early return is the live branch, and a live section can never set `cssOn`.
- **Refusal mid-stream:** `refuse()` is a counted `message()`. The in-app gate does not release the program, and the recorded harness writes a `.refusal`, not a `.nc`. No half-posted program comes out.
- **Bare `G97` with no S word:** it always comes after the stop. On Fanuc the speed held at the switch is the CSS rpm of the moment, and it is harmless because the spindle is stopped. On LinuxCNC (Tormach), a G97 with no S reads the stored S as rpm, which would be the old surface value (for example 200), again with the spindle stopped. Neither matters, because every spindle restart in both posts writes its own S: `G97 S<rpm> M03`, `G96 S.. M03`, or the live `spindleOn S<rpm>`. Neither script ever writes an `M03` / `M3` without an S. I see no need for `G97 S<rpm>`.
- **Tormach tail:** the order is `M9` / `M5` / `G97` / `G30` / `M30`, each on its own line, so there is no same-line block-order question. The home comes after G97 as the PR claims, pinned by `css_arcs_part_load_and_a_trip_home_speak_linuxcnc`.
- **G50 clamp:** the next G96 section writes a new `G50 S` whenever its cap (the lower of machine and tool, with the chuck limit arriving as the section's `MaxSpindleSpeed`) differs from the clamp in force (`fanuc-lathe.cps:409`). `sMax` resets every section. `lathe_workholding_rpm` is green.

### Posted lines per case (Fanuc lathe, from the tests on the merged tree)
- **CSS then live** (`css_then_live.nc`): `G96 S200 M03` ... `M9` / `M05` / `G97` / `(OPERATION: Cross mill - G54)` / `G54` / `T0202` / `G98` / `M1001` / `M1003 S3000`, ending `M1004` / `M1002` / `G99` / `G28 U0 W0` / `M30`.
- **CSS then drill on centre:** `M05` / `G97` / `G54` / `(T0202 DRILL-6)` / `T0202` / `G97 S500 M03` / `M8` / `G00 X0 Z22` / `G83 Z10 F0.2` / `G80` / `M9` / `M05` / `G28 U0 W0`. The drill states its own rpm. No G96 comes back.
- **CSS then G32 thread:** `M05` / `G97` / `G54` / `(T0303 THREAD-60)` / `T0303` / `G97 S400 M03` / ... / `G32 Z9 F2` / `G32 Z8 F2`. The thread runs at constant rpm and never re-enters G96.
- **Two CSS sections:** `G96 S200 M03` / ... / `M05` / `G97` / ... / `T0202` / `G96 S200 M03` / ... / `M05` / `G97` / `G28 U0 W0` / `M30`. This is the flip the decision file describes. It is harmless because the spindle is stopped when it happens.
- **Byte-identity:** `git diff origin/main...head --stat -- crates/app/tests/golden crates/post/tests/recorded` changes exactly one existing golden, `nc/fanuc-lathe/facing_css.nc` (+1 `G97`). The rest are the new `css_then_live` case files. Every other golden passes unchanged.

### Modal groups going into the live section (Fanuc lathe, live branch `liveStart` / `endPreamble`)
| Group | Where it is stated or cancelled | Relies on luck? |
|---|---|---|
| Spindle mode G96/G97 | `G97` at the CSS section's end (this PR) | no |
| Feed mode G98/G99 | `G98` stated at live start (`:509`), `G99` restored at live end (`:465`) | no |
| Plane G18 | header `G21 G18 G40 G80 G99`, never changed. Live sections post straight G01 only, arcs are refused by name (`:681`) | no: no plane-dependent word is posted |
| Nose comp G40/G41/G42 | header `G40`. `onRadiusCompensation` always refuses, so G41/G42 is never posted | no |
| Canned cycle G80 | `G80` at the end of any section that opened a cycle (`:454`). A cycle inside a live section is refused (`:792`) | no |
| C-axis mode | the machine's `c_axis_on` / `c_axis_off`, otherwise refused by name | no |
| Main spindle | `M05` at the previous section's end | no |
| G50 clamp | stays in force. It caps only under G96, and the live spindle is not G96 | harmless, as the script says |
| Units / WCS | `G21` in the header, the WCS stated per section | no |

The fixture `crates/post/tests/recorded/machines/millturn-live.mch` lives under the test tree, not `assets/machines/`, and its placeholder words M1001-M1004 are documented as test-bench codes in `recorded/mod.rs`. It cannot be picked up as a shipped machine. The other ten posts refuse the case by name: the engine refuses posts without `liveTooling` (`"... this post script does not declare liveTooling - use a lathe post that voices the C axis"`), and each script adds its own posed-move refusal. `git grep G96 assets/posts` finds only the two lathe posts.

### Laws
No Rust product code changes; the test code is tests-only. Process: one conventional `fix(post):` commit, a `Changelog:` line, ends `Fixes #1173`, a decision file in `docs/decisions/`, no CHANGELOG/snapshot/PROCESS_VERSION files touched (none needed).

### Notes (not blocking)
1. **Pre-existing, outside this diff:** the live-tool branch of `endPreamble` (`fanuc-lathe.cps:461-469`) returns before `afterOp()`. A live section's Optional stop / Program stop / Go home ask is not written at its end, and `afterAsk` carries over to the next turning section's end. The same code is on main. It deserves its own issue, because a stop the user asked for is silently skipped. I have not filed it.
2. `css_then_live.nc` posts `G50 S10000` then `G50 S3000` on consecutive lines: the machine clamp once, then the tool's lower one. This is #891's existing behaviour and only cosmetic.
3. The recorded stream header still reads `; HSMW-CNC v1`. That is the existing stream-format tag, not this PR.

### What only a real control can prove
- That a specific mill-turn Fanuc (0i-TF / 31i-B with a live spindle) reads the live `S` under G97 as live-spindle rpm, not as the main spindle's S or as `S2=` / `M` spindle-select. That depends on the builder.
- That a bare `G97` after `M05` leaves no stored rpm that a later bare `M03` would pick up. Both posts never write one, but a hand-edited program might.
- PathPilot's acceptance of a bare `G97` line. LinuxCNC documents it as legal.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
